why: The subject lives in Europe/Berlin and is travelling in Tokyo. They step on the scale at 00:30 local, half an hour into 10 August where they are standing. §3.6 folds a weigh-in onto the local day of the timestamp's OWN offset, so it belongs to 2026-08-10.

checks.dayAssignment: Both wrong readings collapse to the same visible error. Converting to UTC gives 2026-08-09T15:30Z, and reading it in the document's timeZone gives 2026-08-09T17:30+02:00 — either way the mass lands on the existing 2026-08-09 day and this case restores one day instead of two.
checks.timeZoneIsNotTheFoldingRule: `timeZone` is the subject's home zone and is deliberately NOT Asia/Tokyo here. A consumer that folds by the document's timeZone rather than by each timestamp's offset cannot pass this case.
checks.dayWithNoFood: 2026-08-10 has no entries at all. A weigh-in alone still makes a day real, so it must appear with entryCount 0 and no energy.
